requirements.subject: ent:metacharacter-symbol
requirements.canonical: A metacharacter symbol IS a symbol that can appear as a lexical mark in a metacharacter definition.
requirements.original: The symbols that can appear as lexical marks in metacharacter definitions are called metacharacter symbols.

requirements.subject: ent:metacharacter-symbol
requirements.canonical: The metacharacter symbols ARE the characters "#", "(", ")", "*", "+", "-", "?", "[", "\", "]", "^", "{", "|" and "}".

requirements.subject: ent:metacharacter-symbol
requirements.condition: the metacharacter symbol does not form a valid metacharacter
requirements.canonical: A metacharacter symbol present in a pattern that does not form a valid metacharacter retains its literal value.
requirements.original: When any of the metacharacter symbols are present in a pattern, but do not form a valid metacharacter, they retain their literal value.

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: A format error CANNOT occur during pattern template instantiation.
requirements.original: NOTE: This rule assures that no format error can occur during pattern template instantiation.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: An error caused by an invalid reference CAN still occur during pattern template instantiation.
requirements.original: However, errors caused by invalid references can still appear (see clauses 27.9 and B.1.5.4 for more details).

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: A character pattern MAY be composed from several fragments using the concatenation operation.
requirements.original: Character patterns may be composed from several fragments using the concatenation operation.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern-fragment
requirements.canonical: The fragments of a character pattern SHALL be concatenated before any evaluation of the pattern expression.
requirements.original: The fragments of the pattern shall be concatenated before any evaluation of the pattern expression.

requirements.subject: ent:character-pattern
requirements.canonical: A pattern definition MAY contain references to values or templates.
requirements.original: Pattern definitions may contain references to values or templates.

requirements.subject: ent:value
requirements.canonical: A value or template referenced in a pattern definition SHALL be of the `charstring` or `universal charstring` type.
requirements.original: The referred value or template shall be of the charstring or universal charstring type and it shall contain either a specific value or pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A value or template referenced in a pattern definition SHALL contain either a specific value or a pattern.
requirements.original: The referred value or template shall be of the charstring or universal charstring type and it shall contain either a specific value or pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.condition: the referenced template contains a pattern
requirements.canonical: When a referenced template contains a pattern, the character pattern definition of that pattern IS used as a fragment for creating the new pattern.
requirements.original: When the referenced template contains a pattern, the character pattern definition of this pattern is used as a fragment for creating the new pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A list of characters enclosed by "[" and "]" matches any single character in that list.
requirements.original: A list of characters enclosed by a pair of "[" and "]" matches any single character in that list.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A set expression IS delimited by the "[" and "]" symbols.
requirements.original: The set expression is delimited by the "[" "]" symbols.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A set expression MAY specify character ranges using the hyphen "-" as separator, in addition to character literals.
requirements.original: In addition to character literals, it is possible to specify character ranges using the hyphen "-" as separator.

requirements.subject: ent:character-range
requirements.canonical: A character range consists of the character immediately before the separator, the character immediately after it, and all characters with a character code between the codes of these two bordering characters.
requirements.original: The range consist of the character immediately before the separator, the character immediately after it and all characters with a character code between the codes of the two bordering characters.

ambiguity.issue: "consist" should be "consists"; "range" means character range in a set expression.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hyphen
requirements.canonical: A hyphen "-" inside a set expression without a preceding or following character loses its special meaning.
requirements.original: A hyphen character "-" inside the list but without preceding or following character loses its special meaning.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A set expression MAY be negated by placing the caret "^" as the first character after the opening square bracket.
requirements.original: The set expression can also be negated by placing the caret "^" character as the first character after the opening square bracket.

requirements.subject: ent:negated-set-expression
requirements.canonical: Negation takes precedence over character ranges in a set expression.
requirements.original: Negation takes precedence over character ranges.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hyphen
requirements.canonical: A hyphen "-" immediately following a negating caret "^" SHALL be processed as a literal character.
requirements.original: Therefore a hyphen "-" immediately following a negating caret "^" shall be processed as a literal character.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-repetition
requirements.canonical: The postfix metacharacter `#(n, m)` matches the preceding expression at least n times but no more than m times.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: #(n, m); Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the preceding expression at least n times but no more than m times (postfix). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-repetition
requirements.canonical: For indexing, the metacharacter `#(n, m)` includes the preceding expression.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: #(n, m); Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the preceding expression at least n times but no more than m times (postfix). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

ambiguity.issue: Table B.1 does not define what the "Indexing" column means; it most likely describes how far the metacharacter extends when positions/groups of a pattern are counted (e.g. for the regexp function). That reading was chosen.
readings: For indexing, the metacharacter `#(n, m)` includes the preceding expression.
The "Indexing" entry describes which characters of the pattern are counted as one item when the preceding-expression postfix metacharacters (#(n,m), #n, +) are applied.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hash-n
requirements.canonical: The postfix metacharacter `#n`, where n is a single digit, matches the preceding expression exactly n times and is equivalent to `#(n)`.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: #n; Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the previous expression exactly n times (where n is a single digit) (postfix); the same as #(n). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

ambiguity.issue: The row says "previous expression" while the other rows say "preceding expression".

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hash-n
requirements.canonical: For indexing, the metacharacter `#n` includes the preceding expression.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: #n; Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the previous expression exactly n times (where n is a single digit) (postfix); the same as #(n). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

The "Indexing" entry describes which characters of the pattern are counted as one item when the preceding-expression postfix metacharacters (#(n,m), #n, +) are applied.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-plus
requirements.canonical: The postfix metacharacter `+` matches the preceding expression one or more times and is equivalent to `#(1,)`.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: +; Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the preceding expression one or several times (postfix); the same as #(1,). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-plus
requirements.canonical: For indexing, the metacharacter `+` includes the preceding expression.
requirements.original: Metacharacter: +; Indexing: Including the preceding expression; Description: Match the preceding expression one or several times (postfix); the same as #(1,). See clause B.1.5.3 for more details
